Add a proximity transition column to differential proximity results

add_proximity_transition.Rd

Classifies the reference/rest and target group medians into proximity regimes around zero ("anti" for < -tau, "random" for [-tau, tau], and "coloc" for > tau) and combines them into a transition column formatted as "<ref_state> -> <tgt_state>".

Usage

add_proximity_transition(
  data,
  tau = 0.15,
  tgt_col = "med_tgt",
  ref_col = NULL,
  transition_col = "transition",
  separator = " -> "
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame or tbl_df returned by DifferentialProximityAnalysis or FindAllProximityMarkers.

tau

Non-negative numeric threshold defining the neutral "random" zone [-tau, tau] around 0. Default is 0.15.

tgt_col

Name of the target median column. Default is "med_tgt".

ref_col

Name of the reference median column. When NULL (default), automatically uses "med_ref" or "med_rest" if present in data.

transition_col

Name of the output transition column. Default is "transition".

separator

Separator placed between the reference and target states. Default is " -> ".

Value

data with a character column named by transition_col. An existing column of that name is replaced.

Details

Works on output tables from both DifferentialProximityAnalysis (using med_ref and med_tgt) and FindAllProximityMarkers (using med_rest and med_tgt).

Examples

library(dplyr)
df <- tibble(
  target = c("B", "CD4 T", "NK"),
  med_tgt = c(0.8, 0.9, -0.4),
  med_rest = c(0.0, 0.5, 0.0),
  diff_median = med_tgt - med_rest
)
add_proximity_transition(df, tau = 0.15)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   target med_tgt med_rest diff_median transition     
#>   <chr>    <dbl>    <dbl>       <dbl> <chr>          
#> 1 B          0.8      0           0.8 random -> coloc
#> 2 CD4 T      0.9      0.5         0.4 coloc -> coloc 
#> 3 NK        -0.4      0          -0.4 random -> anti
